sections.name: Why You Get a Fever
lines: When you get a fever, your body is turning up the heat on purpose.
Germs get in, and your immune cells release chemical messengers.
They travel to your hypothalamus, your brain's thermostat, and it turns the setting up.
Now your normal temperature feels too cold. So you shiver and get the chills, to make more heat.
Many germs struggle in the heat, and some of your immune cells work faster.
When the fight's over, the thermostat resets, and you sweat to cool down.
A very high fever needs a doctor. But a mild one means your body is fighting back.
